title: Operational safeguards and shadow validation for KV cache INT8/FP8 ensembles
creator: Maya Singh
description: Goal: Build a safe, observable, and automatable rollout path for INT8/FP8 quantized KV cache profiles that lets us run production traffic in shadow mode, detect regressions automatically, and apply runtime safeties (gating, fallback) without manual intervention. Scope: (1) implement shadow-serve pipeline for KV cache quant profiles (INT8, FP8, hybrid ensembles); (2) per-request and per-layer drift detectors and PSIs; (3) automated rollback triggers and runtime fallback to FP16/FP32 for flagged requests; (4) synthetic drift injection harness and a validation suite comparing against float baseline on accuracy and tail latency targets. Success metrics: maintain <=0.5% absolute drop in top-line quality (perplexity/nlg BLEU/ROUGE as applicable) vs float baseline on holdout prompt sets, 95th percentile latency within 1.15x of baseline (target: 95p <= 40ms on p4d-like machines), no customer-visible degradation in A/B canaries for 48h. Deliverables: shadowing infra, dashboard panels, calibration automation scripts, playbook describing rollout and rollback conditions.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Maya Singh: Created ticket. Motivation: recent INT8/FP8 KV experiments show promising cost wins but intermittent accuracy drift on long-context tails. We need a production-grade validation and ops pathway before enabling wider rollout.

2025-02-14 - Omar R. Patel: Ran initial ensemble calibration across three models (Llama-2-7B-kv, Llama-2-13B-kv, internal-rlf). Observations: INT8 reduced memory footprint ~2.3x, FP8 showed slightly better quality on prefix-heavy workloads, but INT8 had high variance on certain attention heads. Logged per-head scale histograms to S3: gs://redwood-quant/eng/ENG-51329/initial-hists.tar.gz.

2025-02-18 - Design review (Lena Martinez): Requested clear UX for operators to opt into shadow runs and to toggle fallback heuristics per-customer. Suggested exposing an 'error budget' slider for gradual rollout.

2025-02-20 - Omar R. Patel: Implemented shadow RPC proxy that duplicates requests to quantized path and float baseline; added lightweight sampling to avoid full double-charge. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218. Note: collected 60k shadowed requests; initial comparison shows median logprob delta 0.002, but 0.8% of requests exceed safety threshold (delta > 0.05).

2025-02-24 - Data science (Priya Nair): Built validation harness that computes per-request metrics: token-wise logprob delta, sequence-level BLEU/ROUGE where available, and a calibrated PSI for activation distributions. Notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/kv-quant/ENG-51329/validation-harness.ipynb.

2025-02-26 - Omar R. Patel: Added runtime gating prototype: if per-request predicted drift score > 0.6 OR token-level delta exceeds threshold at early tokens, fallback to FP16 fast-path. Microbenchmark: fallback overhead ~2ms; reduces visible errors by 72% in sample set.

2025-02-28 - Ops (Ethan Zhao): Dashboard panels added to Console beta: 'KV Quant Shadowing' with per-model error-rate, PSI drift, 95p latency, and fallback rate. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/kv-quant/ENG-51329.

2025-03-01 - PM (Anya Brooks): Decided rollout plan: 1) internal canary (shadow only) 2) customer opt-in (shadow + gated live) 3) gradual percentage rollout with automated rollback on safety triggers. Need final acceptance criteria and playbook before opt-in stage.
Next steps: finalize acceptance criteria, run 72h continuous shadow test with synthetic drift injection, finalize PR for shadow proxy and gating, schedule security review for runtime fallback path.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow pipeline in prod stage that mirrors selected routes to quantized KV profiles without affecting live responses (traffic duplication with sampling).
Automated per-request drift scoring computed in <5ms additional wall time and exposed as telemetry.

Defined and implemented rollback triggers: (a) sustained quality regression >0.5% on holdout set for 1h, (b) >1% of requests with token-wise logprob delta >0.05 over 30m, (c) 95p latency >1.2x baseline for 15m.
Playbook documenting operator steps for opt-in/out and emergency rollback, with runbooks and contacts.
Dashboard panels and alerts wired to PagerDuty with example thresholds and run simulation data available.
Synthetic drift harness and validation suite run end-to-end and produce reproducible reports comparing INT8/FP8 ensembles vs float baseline.
